Ukraine Strikes Major Oil Refinery in Tatarstan as Drone Barrage Hits Russia — Ukraine struck the TANЕCO oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with Ukrainian-made FP-1 drones, according to defense company Fire Point. Russian monitoring channels reported at least 12 deaths. The overnight barrage also targeted an oil terminal and power substation, further hitting Russia’s critical energy infrastructure.

Russia Targets Ukraine-Moldova Border Checkpoint as Moscow Unleashes a Multi-Layered Attack — Russia launched a massive overnight attack involving ballistic and cruise missiles and 168 Shahed-type drones. Ukraine’s Air Force said it intercepted most cruise missiles and drones, while Zelensky called for more Patriot interceptors amid deadly strikes across several regions.

Ukraine May Have Left 2 Russian Frigates Unable to Launch Missiles After Novorossiysk Strike — Satellite imagery reportedly shows serious damage to Russia’s Admiral Makarov and Admiral Essen after Ukraine’s Aug. 12 strike on Novorossiysk. Russian and Ukrainian OSINT sources claim both frigates suffered damage to their missile-launch and combat-control systems, though the extent remains unconfirmed.

Fedorov vs Zelensky? Ukraine Entering a New Political Season? — The Verkhovna Rada has appointed a defense minister, and, as expected, Mykhailo Fedorov was not returned to the post. He has recorded a video address criticizing the current system and, conroversially, calling for elections.

‘People, Not Robots’: Ukraine’s Soldiers Justify Human Role Amid Drone Revolution — Drones now destroy about 90% of targets in Ukraine, making traditional airborne assaults increasingly impractical. Yet newly trained paratroopers say demanding physical and psychological training remains vital because technology cannot replace the soldiers who ultimately hold territory.

Ukraine: A Dismissed Innovative Defense Minister Calls for Elections — Fedorov has called for a secure way to hold elections during the war, warning democracy cannot depend on Russia. Critics see the move as a potential campaign launch and warn political turmoil could threaten Ukraine’s defense capabilities.

Hungary Drops Money Laundering Case Against Oschadbank Cash Convoy — Hungary's National Tax and Customs Administration has closed its money laundering case against Oschadbank's cash convoy, finding the seized banknotes and gold originated from a legitimate interbank deal with Raiffeisen Bank International. Lawyer Lóránt Horváth said the closure undercuts Budapest's original justification for the March seizure and detention of seven Ukrainian couriers.

At Least 6 Kyiv Markets Damaged or Destroyed in Russian Attacks Since 2022 — Ten days after a Russian strike devastated Kyiv’s Pochaina flea market, vendors are selling salvaged goods on the street as they struggle to rebuild their livelihoods.

Zelensky Tasks New Defense Minister Khmara With Expanding Ukraine’s Deep Strikes — President Volodymyr Zelensky has tasked newly appointed Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara with expanding long-range strikes, boosting air defense and reforming defense procurement and frontline supply.

Zelensky Names 29-Year-Old Former Schoolteacher Hero of Ukraine After Drone-Zone Rescue — Former teacher Vladyslav Polskyi, now an assault company commander, received Ukraine’s highest honor after personally evacuating two wounded soldiers under Russian drone threat.

Massive Russian Missile and Drone Attack on Kyiv Kills 13, Injures 33, Hits Hospital, School and Homes — Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic and Kalibr missiles and jet-powered drones, killing 13 and injuring 33 as homes, a hospital and school were damaged.

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Ukraine Repels 189 Combat Clashes as Pokrovsk Axis Sees Heaviest Fighting During 24-Hour Period — The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) repelled 189 combat clashes nationwide over the past 24 hours, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk axis, where Russian forces launched 26 assaults. The General Staff reported at least 33 Russian troops killed and 15 wounded in that sector alone.

Ukraine’s Government Removes Sense Bank Chairman Amid Anti-Corruption Probe — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced Wednesday, Aug. 19, that the government removed the chairman of state-owned Sense Bank’s supervisory board, seeking to oust its CEO next. The decision follows a NABU investigation that claimed bank officials helped launder HR. 150 million (roughly $3.3 million) to post bail for a suspect in an earlier corruption case.

Ukraine's Ex-Defense Chief Makes Risky Bet by Entering Electoral Politics — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov delivered a video address on Tuesday, Aug. 18, that called for wartime elections. Even his own supporters distanced themselves from the move, calling it a risky departure from his role as a reformer.

Stray Drone Crashes Into Turkish Police Station in Black Sea Port City Trabzon — A suspected drone crashed into the yard of a police station in Turkey’s Black Sea port city of Trabzon on Tuesday, Aug. 18, damaging four vehicles and shattering windows. No one was injured, but the authorities have launched an investigation into the aircraft’s origin.

Former Deputy Office Head Iryna Mudra Detained Overnight in Corruption Probe — Iryna Mudra, former deputy head of Ukraine’s Presidential Office, was detained on Wednesday, Aug. 19, and is currently undergoing investigative actions at the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU). According to Member of Parliament Oleksiy Honcharenko, Mudra will spend the night in a temporary detention facility.

Russian ‘Banderol’ Type Drone Strikes Zhytomyr Police Building, Kills 3, Injures 53 — A Russian “Banderol”-type drone struck Zhytomyr’s regional police headquarters on Wednesday, Aug. 19, killing 3 and injuring at least 53 people. National Police chief Maksym Tsutskiridze called the strike deliberate terror against those who protect civilians.

Putin Says Russian Economy Remains Stable Despite Attacks — Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia’s economic performance remained positive despite what he described as “terrorist” attacks on infrastructure. Speaking at a meeting on strategic development and national projects on Wednesday, Aug. 19, Putin said damaged logistics and storage facilities required reconstruction and called for measures to support financially strained regions.

Cultural Sovereignty and Agency: Ukraine’s 35-Year Journey to Reclaim Its Voice — For centuries, Russia sought to subsume Ukrainian identity into its own imperial narrative. Since 1991, Ukraine has steadily reclaimed its cultural voice. Russia’s full-scale war accelerated that process, demonstrating that culture is not decoration but a pillar of national security, sovereignty, and international agency.

Zelensky Sacks Deputy Office Head Iryna Mudra After NABU’s New ‘Forrest Gump’ Probe — Zelensky dismissed Iryna Mudra, the deputy head of the Presidential Office tasked with judicial reforms, shortly after the anti-graft agencies announced a new probe dubbed “Forrest Gump” targeting top officials, with Mudra among those reportedly implicated.

On Fedorov, Zelensky, Elections, and the Political Crisis — The first missed elections were for the Verkhovna Rada. And the first post-war elections should also be for the legislature, so that we can exit the war calmly, ensure a smooth transition of power, create a competitive environment primarily for the governing institution of peacetime, and form a government based on programs of action rather than rearranging chairs in offices.

Ukraine – What Is Fedorov Thinking? — Elections will likely just accentuate divisions in Ukrainian society – to be exploited by Putin, which is why Putin is pushing for them. And even Fedorov raising the issue now will signal division.

Russians Lured Into War With Wildberries, Ozon Warehouse Security Jobs — Russian job seekers are reportedly being lured into military service through fake warehouse security vacancies. Verstka found around 2,000 ads offering to guard Wildberries and Ozon facilities, with recruiters promising civilian work while actually proposing one-year defense ministry contracts.

Ukraine Arrests 2 Middle Eastern Men for Sabotaging Substation in Chernivtsi — The SBU said it arrested two men from an unspecified Middle Eastern country in western Ukraine’s Chernivtsi for setting a substation ablaze under the instructions of Russian intelligence. The episode marked a rare occurrence in which foreign nationals are named in similar schemes, though it is not without precedent.

Second Ukrainian Suspect in Nord Stream Case Arrested in Croatia — On Wednesday, German prosecutors said that Ukrainian national Vladimir Z. had been arrested in Pula, Croatia, over his alleged role in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions. Prosecutors accuse him of being part of a group led by former Ukrainian army officer Serhii K. that allegedly planted explosives on Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 near Denmark.

Ukraine Emerges From the Shadows of History as a Shaper of the New World Order — After centuries of struggle, Ukraine is moving from an object of others’ history toward becoming one of the architects creating a new global security order.

Verkhovna Rada Approves Sybiha as Foreign Minister With 266 Votes — Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada on Wednesday, Aug. 19, approved Andriy Sybiha as foreign minister, with 266 lawmakers voting in favor. Sybiha continued leading the Foreign Ministry during the government reshuffle but had temporarily served as acting minister before President Volodymyr Zelensky formally submitted his candidacy to the Ukrainian legislature, the Verkhovna Rada. The ministry said its priorities include strengthening intern

Iran Eyes US Military Targets in Europe if War Escalates — Iranian forces have considered striking US military targets in southeastern Europe and Cyprus if President Donald Trump escalates the war, according to people close to the Iranian regime cited by the Financial Times. Tehran has also examined attacks on subsea fiber-optic cables in the Strait of Hormuz and warned that any renewed US offensive could trigger retaliation beyond the Middle East.

Ukraine Says Russian ‘Safari’ Attack on Minibus Kills Four — A Russian drone strike on a minibus in frontline Kherson killed four civilians and wounded five others Wednesday, Ukrainian officials said. Kyiv accused Russian forces of conducting a “safari”-style hunt targeting civilians in the southern city, which faces frequent drone attacks from Russian positions across the Dnipro River.

BlueBird Tech Unveils Bebradrone-M UAV for Training Ukraine’s Interceptor Drone Operators — Ukraine’s BlueBird Tech has unveiled the Bebradrone-M, a fixed-wing UAV designed to train pilots and interceptor drone operators using real aerial targets. The drone can simulate reconnaissance aircraft and decoys, allowing teams to practice detection, pursuit and interception in scenarios designed to replicate battlefield conditions.

Ukraine Picks General to Run Defense Ministry as Civilian Status Rule Sparks Questions — Ukraine’s parliament appointed Maj. Gen. Yevhen Khmara as defense minister with 312 votes, following weeks of protests over Fedorov’s dismissal. Khmara’s appointment also faced a legal hurdle because Ukrainian law requires the defense minister to be a civilian.

Ukraine, Russia Swap 103 Prisoners Each in Latest Exchange — Ukraine and Russia exchanged 103 prisoners each on Aug. 19, bringing 103 Ukrainian soldiers home from Russian captivity. The released Ukrainians include troops from the Armed Forces, Border Guard Service, and National Guard who fought in Mariupol and across several regions.

Moscow Gas Stations Impose Fuel Limits as Russian Shortage Deepens — Moscow gas stations are rationing gasoline and diesel as a widening fuel shortage puts pressure on Russia’s capital, while authorities scramble to redirect supplies from other regions.

Trump Scales Back Joint Drills With South Korea — Trump’s decision to scale back US-South Korea military exercises has raised concerns about the consequences for regional security. Critics argue he overestimates his relationship with Kim Jong-un, potentially strengthening North Korea’s regime and aggression. Germany’s Süddeutsche Zeitung warns that the move could weaken Seoul’s trust in Washington and push South Korea toward new alliances.

NABU Starts ‘Forrest Gump’ Operation, Uncovers Crisis Plan — Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office are conducting a special operation targeting an alleged criminal organization led by a current and former lawmaker. During searches, investigators found a document outlining a crisis communication plan related to a Verkhovna Rada temporary investigative commission.

Open the Black Sea for Shipping! — The Russo-Ukrainian War is heating up in the Black Sea this summer, with tit-for-tat attacks on shipping. The Ukrainian economy is at risk and needs the help of Europeans, particularly the Baltic states.

Ukraine Needs Allies, Not Amnesia: Viktor Yushchenko in Azerbaijan — Former President Viktor Yushchenko’s visit to Azerbaijan drew criticism over his warm relationship with Ilham Aliyev. The controversy highlights a broader tension between Kyiv’s need for strategic partners and the democratic principles associated with the Orange Revolution and Maidan.

NATO Draws Up 3-Step Plan to Fight Russia if Putin Attacks the Baltics — NATO has reportedly developed a three-part strategy for a potential Russian attack on the Baltic states. According to Bild, the plan includes suppressing Russian missile systems, deploying autonomous drones along NATO’s borders and striking key military and logistical targets inside Russia.

EXPLAINER: 35 Years Ago Today, the World Held Its Breath — On this day in 1991, a failed hardline coup in Moscow became the final shock that pushed Ukraine from asserted sovereignty to independence. As Soviet authority faltered, Ukraine’s democratic forces, sovereignty Communists led by Leonid Kravchuk, and public protests in Kyiv, converged against a crumbling empire. Within days, the coup’s collapse cleared the way for parliament to meet on Aug. 24 and declare an independent Ukrainian state.

‘Zero Tolerance’: Polish Woman Charged After Alleged Nationality-Based Attack on Ukrainian Siblings — A 46-year-old Polish woman has been charged after allegedly verbally and physically attacking two Ukrainian siblings, aged 14 and 12, in Bydgoszcz. Police say the incident involved nationality-based insults and damage to the children’s toy drone.

Major Explosives Plant Hit Again as Ukrainian Drones Strike Across Russia Overnight — Ukrainian drones targeted the Sverdlov explosives plant in Dzerzhinsk, according to Russian and OSINT reports, marking another attack on the facility this year. Overnight strikes were also reported in Ufa, the Tula region, and near Moscow, with casualties reported in Ufa.

Estonia Probes Possible Russian Sabotage After Fire at Defense Firm Supplying Ukraine — Estonia is investigating whether Russia was behind a suspected arson attack on Milrem Robotics, whose unmanned military systems are used in Ukraine.

2 Killed, 10 Wounded as Russia Hits Zaporizhzhia Region 1,019 Times in 24 Hours — Russian forces carried out 1,019 attacks across 52 settlements in the Zaporizhzhia region, including 717 drone strikes, 19 airstrikes and 276 artillery attacks. Two people were killed and 10 wounded.

Lavrov Threatens UK With ‘Consequences’ Over Ukraine War — Sergei Lavrov says Moscow could treat British involvement in Ukrainian strikes on Russia as participation in the war, escalating an earlier embassy warning to London.

Fedorov Calls for Wartime Elections, Says Putin Shouldn’t Set the Timeline — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for Ukraine to develop a mechanism to hold elections during the war, arguing Russia should not be able to dictate when Ukrainian citizens vote. His remarks came hours after President Volodymyr Zelensky nominated a permanent replacement for the post on Aug, 18.

Russian Strike Halts DTEK Thermal Power Plant — Russia carried out a massive strike on a DTEK thermal power plant in Ukraine on Tuesday, Aug. 18, forcing the station to halt electricity generation. According to DTEK, its thermal power plants have been attacked more than 230 times since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022.

Russian Jet-Powered ‘Shahed’ Drone Reaches Western Ukraine for First Time — A Russian jet-powered “Shahed” drone flew roughly 900 kilometers (nearly 560 miles) from Crimea into western Ukraine on Tuesday, Aug. 18, marking the farthest such strike recorded so far. According to Ukrainian monitoring systems, the flight path was designed to avoid air defenses.

Ukraine, Belgium Advance Talks on Drone Deal — President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed possible signing dates with Belgian Deputy Prime Minister Maxime Prévot on Tuesday, Aug. 18, as Ukraine and Belgium move forward with finalizing a Drone Deal.

Germany Opens Drone Defense Research Center After Leipzig Airport Incident — Germany opened a new drone security research center on Tuesday, Aug. 18, less than two weeks after an explosive-laden unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) was found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig-Halle Airport. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called the incident part of a broader hybrid threat pattern linked to Russia.

Stun Grenade Injures 4 in Russian School After Counter-Terrorism Exercise Goes Wrong — Russian media said four teachers were injured in a school in the Moscow region after law enforcement accidentally lobbed a stun grenade into a room during an anti-terrorism drill. Similar exercises began in 2024, with the same year marked by the infamous Crocus concert hall shooting in Moscow that killed over 100.

Kanye West to Perform 2 Shows in Russia’s St. Petersburg This October — US pop-star Kanye West announced two concerts in Russia St. Petersburg in October, with tickets ranging 9,000-160,000 rubles ($106-$1,880) sold out in hours as local agencies reported massive spike in train and hotel searches. A Russian producer said it is likely to bring about a boost in Russia’s tourism revenues.

Zelensky Submits Khmara, Sybiha Nominations to Parliament — Presidential submissions naming Yevhenii Khmara as defense minister and Andriy Sybiha as foreign minister have been submitted to Ukraine’s parliament, according to Ukrainian lawmakers. Both officials currently serve as acting heads of their ministries. Parliament is expected to consider the nominations on Wednesday, Aug. 19.

Controversial Ukrainian Lawmaker Bezuhla Returns to Servant of the People Party — Mariana Bezuhla has returned to the Servant of the People legislative party after leaving it in summer 2024. Two other Servant of the People lawmakers, Bohdan Morklianyk and Viktoriia Reznikova, also took their oaths on Aug. 18 after entering the Verkhovna Rada to replace lawmakers who became ministers.

Russia Punishes Fuel Shortage Protesters as Fuel Crisis Worsens — Russians are facing fines and detention for publicly protesting gasoline shortages, with authorities labeling complaints as unauthorized rallies or illegal campaigning. The crackdown comes as fuel restrictions spread across regions amid refinery disruptions and declining gasoline supplies.

Big Ukraine Terrain Gains, Novorossiysk Smacked Hard, NATO Ups the Appeasement — Ukraine formally confirmed a three-month southern offensive that's retaken 350+ sq km near Hulyaipole, while Russia pounded Kyiv and Odesa with missiles and drones. The war's biggest naval strike hit Novorossiysk, damaging four warships and shutting down all three grain terminals, prompting Ukraine to offer Russia a Black Sea maritime ceasefire. Meanwhile, AFU command shakeups continue, Turkey sold Kyiv ATACMS and M

Odesa Enlistment Service Members Accused of Abuse in Mobilization — Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation says it uncovered alleged abuse by two notification groups from a district Territorial Recruitment and Social Support Center in Odesa region. Ten military personnel allegedly used force, beat civilians, deployed tear gas and forcibly took people to the center. Investigators have documented 15 incidents, including one case in which a man fleeing the group was hit by a service vehicle.

US Awards Raytheon $22.9 Billion Deal to Boost Tomahawk — The US military has awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion, seven-year contract to expand Tomahawk missile production from 60 to more than 1,000 annually. The deal comes as Washington seeks to rebuild depleted stocks after supplying weapons to allies and using munitions in the Iran conflict.

Khmara Set for Defense Minister Vote Despite Questions Over His Military Status — The Verkhovna Rada is expected to vote Wednesday on the appointments of Khmara as defense minister and Sybiha as foreign minister. Maj. Gen. Khmara’s expected nomination comes amid questions over the legal requirement for the defense minister to be a civilian.

Ships Not Entering Odesa Ports: What This Means for Ukraine’s Grain Exports — Ship traffic to Greater Odesa collapsed after Russian drone and missile attacks intensified, with just seven vessels entering in the first 11 days of August against 169 in July. USPA blames the drop on rising attack risk, while UCAB estimates Ukraine is losing $450-500 million in export revenue monthly as wheat and barley sell below production cost.

Ukraine Returns Remains of Nationalist Leader Assassinated by Moscow in 1938 — The remains of Colonel Yevhen Konovalets, first head of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) and an officer of the Ukrainian People’s Republic Army, were reinterred at Ukraine’s National Military Memorial Cemetery on Tuesday, Aug. 18, with President Volodymyr Zelensky attending. Konovalets was exhumed from Rotterdam’s Crooswijk cemetery on Aug. 11 and returned to Ukraine two days later. The remains are bur

Russia Has No Plans for Peace Deal This Year, Ukraine Says — HUR Deputy Chief Vadym Skibitsky said Russia does not plan to reach a peace agreement this year and may launch a new mobilization after elections. He also warned of continued attacks on Ukraine’s energy and gas infrastructure.

5 Years Back in Power, the Taliban Has Russia in Its Pocket and Now Eyes the US — Donald Trump negotiated the US withdrawal from Afghanistan; Joe Biden carried it out with catastrophic results. Five years later, the Taliban remains brutally repressive but increasingly difficult to isolate, with Russia formally recognizing its government and Kabul now courting US diplomats and investment.

Protesters Rally Outside Ukrainian Parliament as Defense Minister Vote Hangs in Balance — Dozens of protesters gathered outside Ukraine’s parliament demanding Mykhailo Fedorov’s reinstatement as defense minister. The Rada delayed the start of its session until noon, while an MP said Zelensky had yet to submit a candidate for the post.

Russia’s ‘Dramatic’ Manpower Shortage Is Reshaping Its War Tactics | Bohdan Nahaylo — Russia’s severe manpower shortage is forcing a tactical shift on the Ukrainian front, with troops increasingly using small three- to four-man infiltration groups instead of mass assaults. Kyiv Post Editor-in-Chief Bohdan Nahaylo also warns of intensified ballistic missile strikes ahead of winter.

Russian Missile Strike Kills 10 in Kharkiv Region, Drone Barrage Hits Kyiv — A Russian missile strike on Pechenyhy in the Kharkiv region killed 10 people and injured 18, local authorities said. Russia also launched 147 drones overnight, hitting civilian infrastructure near Kyiv and killing 2 people in Zaporizhzhia.

637 Drones Target Moscow Region as Wildberries Warehouses Suffer Billions in Losses — Russian officials said 637 Ukrainian drones targeted Moscow and the surrounding region overnight on Aug. 17-18, with several people injured and infrastructure damaged. A Wildberries warehouse caught fire, adding to mounting losses from repeated strikes on the e-commerce giant’s logistics network.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 17, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on August 17, 2026

Britain Hits Back at Russian Threats Over Ukraine’s Use of British Drones — Britain rejected Russian threats over Ukraine’s reported use of British-made drones, saying its support for Kyiv will continue.

What Is Happening to Russia’s Rear? How Ukraine Shattered the Kremlin’s Sanctuary — Ukraine’s long-range drone campaign is eroding Russia’s rear-area security, while even Kremlin-controlled television acknowledges the growing reach of Ukrainian strikes.

Melania Trump Helps Reunite Another Child With Family Amid Russia’s War — US First Lady Melania Trump facilitated another family reunification as efforts continue to return children separated by Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Russia Threatens UK Over British-Made Drones Allegedly Used in Ukrainian Deep Strikes — Russia accused Britain of escalating its involvement in the war after reports that UK-made drones were used in Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian territory.

Russia Summons Japanese Ambassador After Tokyo Protests Putin’s Kuril Islands Visit — Russia summoned Japan’s ambassador after Tokyo protested President Vladimir Putin’s visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, escalating an already bitter territorial row.
